payload.title: Observable session manager + drop app-side UserDefaults persistence
payload.description:
## Frick today
More than RangerCRM is using. FrickClient ALREADY auto-persists sessions to the Keychain (FrickKeychainSessionStore) and auto-restores on construction — see FrickClient.swift (~line 1011) and FrickSessionPersistence.swift (FrickSessionPersisting protocol + Keychain/InMemory impls). The client comment even states injecting a session is "no longer required for cross-launch persistence — the client auto-restores."

What Frick does NOT offer: an observable auth-STATE holder (the session/isAuthenticating/verbs shape SwiftUI gates on).

## What RangerCRM built
/Users/bri/dev/RangerCRM/RangerCRM/Model/RangerData/Services/FrickSessionManager.swift — an @Observable holder with `session`, `isAuthenticating`, and signIn/signUp/signOut/requestPasswordReset/resetPassword verbs. BUT it ALSO re-implements session persistence to UserDefaults (restorePersistedSession/persist, ~lines 120-137), which duplicates and arguably REGRESSES Frick's existing Keychain persistence (UserDefaults is not the Keychain).

## What the port gives us (two wins)
1. The observable auth-state wrapper (session/isAuthenticating/verbs) becomes a reusable FrickSwift type every app needs.
2. RangerCRM DELETES its UserDefaults persistence and rides Frick's Keychain auto-restore — strictly more secure, less code. This is the one port that is partly "stop reimplementing what Frick already does."

## Notes
Preserve the DEBUG test initializer pattern (init(forTestingWith:session:) used by RangerCRMTests/Integration/) — the integration suite drives isolated clients/sessions without touching the singleton. Keep the RANGER_UITEST reset hook app-side (it wipes app-specific UserDefaults keys), but the generic session restore/persist moves to (or is deleted in favor of) Frick.
